text:
Maria: noticed a surge of GPU job failures in us-west-2 this morning, lots of ECONNRESET and very long start times
Sam: saw same, jobs queueing, provisioner keeps retrying and hitting node throttles :grimacing:
Lee: reported high iowait on host pool-gpu-azc-*/scratchfs around 07:12 UTC
Kyle: can you paste iostat/top output?
Maria: pasted snippet from one host:
```
% iostat -x 1 3
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
           12.3    0.0    5.1   27.8     0.0   54.8
Device            r/s     w/s    rkB/s    wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         2500.2  410.6  512000.0 32800.0   192.5   35.6   9.8   3.1    12.4    0.4   99.8
```
Lee: avgqu-sz 35 and %util ~100% on nvme0n1, that explains the slow pod startup
Sam: I see repeated fstrim errors in kernel logs too: `fsync: errno=5` then device errors
Maria: smartctl shows rising media_errors and high temp spikes on nvme0n1 at 06:50 UTC
Kyle: so mix of wear and sudden write bursts from batch-prewarm jobs?
Lee: yes — our batch prewarm group runs heavy checkpoint writes to scratch at scale when capacity shifts
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042 (storage iops storm causing GPU pod provisioning latency)
Sam: mitigation idea: throttle prewarm batch job parallelism and pause aggressive cleaner/scrub that runs at 06:30
Maria: cleaner runs at 06:25 across whole fleet, it does parallel trims and background gc — that plus prewarm equals write amplification
Kyle: can we temporarily move prewarm to a different AZ or tag a subset of nodes as no-prewarm?
Lee: easiest is to flip autoscaler policy to avoid scheduling prewarm on hot-ssd nodes; patch deployed in ~5m
Maria: rolling a constraint via infra-config now: `nodeSelector: no-prewarm=true` to prewarm job template
Sam: applying reduced parallelism on prewarm controller: replicas 100 -> 20 (k8s patch applied)
devops-bot: deployment bootstrap-perf-prewarm scaled to 20 replicas by Sam at 07:38 UTC
Lee: also bumped scrub interval to 12h from 1h on the scratch cleaner in the interim
Kyle: good. still need long term: either spread prewarm IO across disks or use remote objectstore for checkpoints
Maria: run `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` output attached — recommends firmware update (FW v2.1.3 -> 2.2.0) and scheduled replacement for drives with >1000 media_errors
Sam: filing hardware ticket to swap hot nodes and request firmware rollouts in batch (avoid rolling all in the same AZ)
Lee: on schedulers: we should add an IO-aware scheduler score so provisioning avoids nodes hitting avgqu thresholds
Maria: agreed. also want to add eviction soft-threshold so we fail fast before provisioning stalls other services
Kyle: tracked follow-ups:
- HW replace list + firmware rollout (Sam)
- IO-aware scheduling prototype (Lee)
- Prewarm redesign to use checkpoint streaming to S3 (Maria)
- Cleaner rate-limiter and backoff heuristics (Kyle)
Sam: created tickets and linked to INC-2026-042: HW-2189, SCHED-334, PREWARM-77, SCRUB-12
Maria: immediate status: queue length stabilizing after scale-down + scrub delay, error rates dropped ~70% in last 20m
devops-bot: metrics alert resolved: nvme_io_high_us-west-2 cleared at 08:02 UTC
Lee: add postmortem and runbook updates: include a step to check `avgqu-sz` and `nvme temp` before any large parallel writes
Maria: will draft postmortem, include command snippets and thresholds (`avgqu-sz > 10` or `%util > 85%` as triggers)
Sam: thumbs up. if anyone sees recurrence ping pager and tag INC-2026-042
Kyle: nice quick coordination, thanks all :heart:
Maria: follow-up meeting in 1d to review prewarm redesign options and rollout plan for firmware/replacements
